3.1.1.title: Topic 3.1.1 · Monomers and Polymers
3.1.1.spec: Monomers, polymers, condensation reactions, hydrolysis reactions

sections.heading: Core Definitions
points: Monomer: A smaller unit from which larger molecules (polymers) are made (e.g. monosaccharides, amino acids, nucleotides).
Polymer: A large molecule made from many repeating similar/identical monomer units joined together (e.g. polysaccharides, polypeptides, polynucleotides).
Condensation reaction: Joins two molecules together with the formation of a chemical bond and involves the elimination of a molecule of water (H2O).
Hydrolysis reaction: Breaks a chemical bond between two molecules and involves the use of a water molecule (H2O).

3.1.2.title: Topic 3.1.2 · Carbohydrates
3.1.2.spec: Monosaccharides, disaccharides, polysaccharides (starch, glycogen, cellulose), biochemical tests

sections.heading: Monosaccharides & Disaccharides
points: Monosaccharides: Glucose (α- and β-isomers), galactose, fructose. Hexose formula: C6H12O6.
α-glucose vs β-glucose: On C1, α-glucose has H above and OH below; β-glucose has OH above and H below.
Glycosidic bond: Formed by condensation between two monosaccharides.
Disaccharides: Maltose (glucose + glucose), Sucrose (glucose + fructose), Lactose (glucose + galactose).

sections.heading: Polysaccharides & Biochemical Tests
points: Starch (plants): Amylose (unbranched, helical α-1,4) + Amylopectin (branched α-1,4 and α-1,6). Insoluble (no osmotic effect), compact, easily hydrolysed.
Glycogen (animals): Highly branched α-glucose (α-1,4 and α-1,6). More ends for rapid hydrolysis to glucose for respiration.
Cellulose (plant cell walls): Straight, unbranched chains of β-glucose (β-1,4). Adjacent chains inverted 180°, linked by hydrogen bonds to form microfibrils (high tensile strength).
Reducing sugars (Benedict's): Heat with Benedict's reagent → brick-red precipitate. Non-reducing (e.g. sucrose): Boil with dilute HCl, neutralise with NaHCO3, re-test with Benedict's.
Starch test: Iodine in potassium iodide solution → orange-brown to blue-black.

3.1.3.title: Topic 3.1.3 · Lipids
3.1.3.spec: Triglycerides, phospholipids, saturated/unsaturated fatty acids, emulsion test

sections.heading: Structure & Properties
points: Triglyceride: 1 glycerol + 3 fatty acids joined by 3 ester bonds via 3 condensation reactions (3 H2O released).
Saturated vs Unsaturated: Saturated has no C=C double bonds; unsaturated has at least one C=C double bond (causes a kink, lowers melting point).
Phospholipid: 1 glycerol + 2 fatty acids + 1 phosphate group. Hydrophilic phosphate head + hydrophobic fatty acid tails → forms phospholipid bilayer in membranes.
Emulsion test: Shake sample with ethanol, then pour into water → milky-white emulsion indicates lipid.

3.1.4.title: Topic 3.1.4 · Proteins & Enzymes
3.1.4.spec: Amino acids, peptide bonds, 1°–4° structure, biuret test, induced fit, inhibitors

sections.heading: Protein Structure & Biuret Test
points: Amino acid: Central C bonded to –NH2, –COOH, –H, and variable R group. Joined by peptide bonds via condensation.

Primary: Sequence of amino acids. Secondary: α-helix or β-pleated sheet held by hydrogen bonds. Tertiary: 3D folding held by H-bonds, ionic bonds, disulfide bridges. Quaternary: ≥2 polypeptide chains (e.g. haemoglobin).
Biuret test: Add NaOH then dilute CuSO4 → blue to purple/lilac.

sections.heading: Enzyme Action & Inhibition
points: Induced fit model: Active site is not rigid; binding of substrate induces a slight conformational change in the active site, straining substrate bonds and lowering activation energy (Ea).
Factors: Temperature (kinetic energy vs denaturation), pH (changes H+/OH- disrupting ionic/H-bonds), substrate/enzyme concentration.
Competitive inhibitor: Similar shape to substrate, binds active site; overcome by increasing substrate concentration.
Non-competitive inhibitor: Binds allosteric site, changes tertiary structure & active site shape; NOT overcome by extra substrate.

3.1.5.title: Topic 3.1.5 · Nucleic Acids & DNA Replication
3.1.5.spec: DNA/RNA nucleotides, phosphodiester bonds, semi-conservative replication, Meselson-Stahl

sections.heading: DNA & RNA Structure
points: Nucleotide: Pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA) + phosphate group + nitrogenous base (A, T/U, C, G).
Phosphodiester bond: Formed by condensation between phosphate of one nucleotide and C3 of pentose sugar of the next.
DNA: Antiparallel double helix; A=T (2 H-bonds), C≡G (3 H-bonds). RNA: Single-stranded, shorter, uracil (U) instead of thymine (T).

sections.heading: Semi-Conservative Replication
points: 1. DNA helicase breaks hydrogen bonds between complementary bases, unwinding the double helix.
2. Both strands act as templates; free DNA nucleotides align by complementary base pairing (A-T, C-G).
3. DNA polymerase joins adjacent nucleotides via phosphodiester bonds (5'→3' direction).
4. Each new DNA molecule contains one original (parent) strand and one newly synthesised strand (proven by Meselson & Stahl using <sup>15</sup>N / <sup>14</sup>N).

3.1.6.title: Topic 3.1.6 · ATP
3.1.6.spec: ATP structure, hydrolysis by ATP hydrolase, resynthesis by ATP synthase

sections.heading: ATP Energy Currency
points: Structure: Ribose sugar + adenine base + 3 phosphate groups.
Hydrolysis: ATP + H2O → ADP + Pi (catalysed by ATP hydrolase), releasing energy in small, manageable amounts; Pi can phosphorylate other compounds to make them more reactive.
Resynthesis: ADP + Pi → ATP + H2O (catalysed by ATP synthase during respiration and photosynthesis).

3.1.7.title: Topic 3.1.7 · Water
3.1.7.spec: Hydrogen bonding and biological properties of water

sections.heading: 5 Key Properties of Water
points: Metabolite: Used in condensation and hydrolysis reactions.
Solvent: Polar molecule dissolves ionic/polar substances for metabolic reactions and transport.
High specific heat capacity: Hydrogen bonds absorb lots of energy before temperature rises → buffers temperature in cells/habitats.
High latent heat of vaporisation: Evaporation (sweating/transpiration) provides efficient cooling with minimal water loss.
Cohesion & surface tension: H-bonds between water molecules allow continuous columns in xylem and support small organisms.

3.1.8.title: Topic 3.1.8 · Inorganic Ions
3.1.8.spec: Roles of H+, Fe2+, Na+, PO4^3- ions

sections.heading: Key Inorganic Ions
points: H+: Determines pH; affects enzyme tertiary structure and haemoglobin affinity.
Fe2+: Haem group in haemoglobin; binds O2 reversibly.
Na+: Co-transport of glucose and amino acids across ileum/nephron membranes; action potentials.
PO43-: Component of DNA/RNA nucleotides, ATP, and phospholipids.

3.2.1.title: Topic 3.2.1 · Cell Structure & Microscopy
3.2.1.spec: Eukaryotic organelles, prokaryotes, viruses, optical/TEM/SEM microscopes, cell fractionation

sections.heading: Cells & Organelles
points: Eukaryotic organelles: Nucleus (nuclear envelope, pores, nucleolus), mitochondria (cristae, matrix), chloroplasts (thylakoids, stroma), RER/SER, Golgi apparatus (modifies/packages proteins into vesicles), lysosomes, 80S ribosomes.
Prokaryotes: No membrane-bound organelles, circular DNA (no histones), plasmids, 70S ribosomes, murein (peptidoglycan) cell wall, optional capsule/flagellum.
Viruses: Acellular, non-living; genetic material (DNA or RNA) + capsid + attachment proteins (+ lipid envelope).

sections.heading: Microscopy & Cell Fractionation
points: Magnification = Image size / Actual size. Resolution = minimum distance apart two objects can be distinguished as separate.

Optical: Low resolution (~200 nm, light wavelength), live specimens, colour. TEM: Highest resolution (~0.1 nm), 2D internal ultrastructure, dead/vacuum. SEM: 3D surface image, lower resolution than TEM.

Cell fractionation: Homogenise tissue in cold (reduces enzyme activity), isotonic (prevents osmotic lysis/shrinking), buffered (maintains pH/protein structure) solution → filter → differential ultracentrifugation (nuclei → chloroplasts → mitochondria → lysosomes → ER → ribosomes).

3.2.2.title: Topic 3.2.2 · Mitosis & the Cell Cycle
3.2.2.spec: Interphase (G1, S, G2), PMAT, cytokinesis, mitotic index, cancer, binary fission

sections.heading: Cell Cycle & Mitosis
points: Interphase: G1 (growth, protein/organelle synthesis), S (DNA replication), G2 (further growth).
Prophase: Chromosomes condense; nuclear envelope breaks down; spindle fibres form.
Metaphase: Chromosomes line up at the cell equator; spindle fibres attach to centromeres.
Anaphase: Centromeres divide; sister chromatids pulled to opposite poles by spindle shortening.
Telophase & Cytokinesis: Chromosomes uncoil; nuclear envelopes reform; cytoplasm divides.
Mitotic index = (Number of cells in mitosis) / (Total number of cells). Uncontrolled cell division leads to tumours/cancer.

3.2.3.title: Topic 3.2.3 · Transport Across Cell Membranes
3.2.3.spec: Fluid-mosaic model, simple/facilitated diffusion, osmosis, active transport, co-transport

sections.heading: Membrane Transport Mechanisms
points: Fluid-mosaic model: Phospholipid bilayer (fluid) with embedded intrinsic/extrinsic proteins, glycoproteins, glycolipids, and cholesterol (regulates fluidity).
Simple diffusion: Passive, down concentration gradient, small/non-polar molecules.
Facilitated diffusion: Passive, via channel or carrier proteins, down concentration gradient.
Osmosis: Net movement of water from higher water potential (Ψ) to lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane.
Active transport: Carrier proteins + ATP hydrolysis, against concentration gradient.

Co-transport (ileum): Na+/K+ pump actively exports Na+ into blood → Na+ diffuses into epithelial cell via co-transporter bringing glucose against its gradient → glucose leaves into blood by facilitated diffusion.

3.2.4.title: Topic 3.2.4 · Cell Recognition & the Immune System
3.2.4.spec: Phagocytosis, T cells, B cells, antibodies, vaccines, herd immunity, HIV, ELISA

sections.heading: Non-Specific & Specific Immunity
points: Phagocytosis: Phagocyte attracted by chemicals → engulfs pathogen into phagosome → fuses with lysosome (lysozymes hydrolyse pathogen) → presents antigens (APC).
Cell-mediated (T cells): Helper T cells (TH) bind APCs, release cytokines to activate cytotoxic T cells (perforin) and B cells.
Humoral (B cells): B cell binds complementary antigen, activated by TH → clonal selection & expansion into plasma cells (secrete monoclonal antibodies) and memory B cells.
Antibody: Quaternary structure (4 polypeptide chains, disulfide bridges), 2 variable antigen-binding sites → agglutination & opsonisation.

sections.heading: Vaccines, HIV & ELISA
points: Vaccination: Introduces antigens → primary response + memory cells → rapid secondary response. Herd immunity protects unvaccinated individuals.
HIV: Retrovirus (RNA + reverse transcriptase) infects TH cells → impairs humoral & cell-mediated immunity → AIDS.
ELISA: Uses monoclonal antibodies linked to an enzyme to detect specific antigens or antibodies via a colour change.

3.3.1.title: Topic 3.3.1 · Surface Area to Volume Ratio
3.3.1.spec: SA:V ratio, metabolic rate, adaptations for exchange

sections.heading: SA:V Principles
points: Smaller organisms have a larger SA:V ratio → greater heat loss per unit body mass → higher metabolic rate.
Large organisms have a small SA:V ratio and long diffusion distances, requiring specialised exchange surfaces and mass transport systems.

3.3.2.title: Topic 3.3.2 · Gas Exchange
3.3.2.spec: Insects, fish gills, xerophytic plants, human lungs and ventilation

sections.heading: Gas Exchange Systems
points: Insects: Spiracles → tracheae → tracheoles (thin walls, short diffusion distance, abdominal pumping).
Fish: Gill filaments + lamellae; countercurrent flow (blood and water flow in opposite directions, maintaining a concentration gradient across the entire gill length).
Plants: Stomata + guard cells. Xerophytes: Thick waxy cuticle, sunken stomata, rolled leaves, hairs, reduced SA:V.
Human lungs: Inspiration (external intercostals + diaphragm contract → thoracic volume ↑ → pressure ↓ below atmospheric). Alveoli: 1 cell thick, huge SA, capillary network.

3.3.3.title: Topic 3.3.3 · Digestion and Absorption
3.3.3.spec: Amylase, membrane-bound disaccharidases, endopeptidases/exopeptidases, lipase, micelles

sections.heading: Enzymatic Digestion & Absorption
points: Carbohydrates: Salivary/pancreatic amylase (starch → maltose) + membrane-bound disaccharidases (maltase, sucrase, lactase).
Proteins: Endopeptidases (hydrolyse internal peptide bonds → more ends), exopeptidases (terminal bonds), membrane-bound dipeptidases.

Lipids: Bile salts emulsify lipids (increase SA); lipase hydrolyses triglycerides → monoglycerides + fatty acids → form micelles → diffuse into epithelial cells → reformed into triglycerides & chylomicrons → lacteals.

3.3.4.title: Topic 3.3.4 · Mass Transport
3.3.4.spec: Haemoglobin & Bohr effect, cardiac cycle, tissue fluid, xylem cohesion-tension, phloem mass flow

sections.heading: Haemoglobin & Circulatory System
points: Haemoglobin: Cooperative binding gives S-shaped dissociation curve. Bohr effect: High pCO2 shifts curve right (lower O2 affinity → more O2 unloaded at respiring tissues).
Cardiac cycle: Atrial systole → ventricular systole (AV valves close, SL valves open) → diastole (SL valves close). CO = HR × SV.

Tissue fluid: High hydrostatic pressure at arteriole end forces fluid out (ultrafiltration); lower hydrostatic pressure & lower water potential (plasma proteins) at venule end draws water back in by osmosis.

sections.heading: Transport in Plants
points: Xylem (cohesion-tension): Evaporation from mesophyll → water potential gradient → tension pulls continuous water column up xylem (cohesion between H2O, adhesion to xylem walls).
Phloem (mass flow): Active loading of sucrose into sieve tubes at source → lowers Ψ → water enters by osmosis → high hydrostatic pressure pushes sap to sink where sucrose is unloaded.

3.4.1.title: Topic 3.4.1 · DNA, Genes and Chromosomes
3.4.1.spec: Prokaryotic vs eukaryotic DNA, introns, exons, genetic code properties

sections.heading: DNA Organisation & Genetic Code
points: Prokaryotes: Short, circular DNA, not associated with histones. Eukaryotes: Long, linear DNA associated with histones to form chromosomes (plus circular DNA in mitochondria/chloroplasts).
Introns vs Exons: Exons code for amino acids; introns are non-coding sequences spliced out of pre-mRNA.
Genetic code: Triplet (codon = 3 bases), degenerate (multiple codons per amino acid), universal, non-overlapping.

sections.heading: Transcription & Translation
points: Transcription: DNA helicase unwinds gene; RNA polymerase joins free RNA nucleotides complementary to template strand → pre-mRNA.
Splicing (eukaryotes): Introns removed, exons joined to form mature mRNA.
Translation: mRNA binds ribosome; tRNA with complementary anticodon brings specific amino acid; ATP used to form peptide bonds; stops at stop codon.

3.4.3.title: Topic 3.4.3 · Mutation & Meiosis
3.4.3.spec: Gene/chromosome mutations, meiosis I & II, crossing over, independent segregation

sections.heading: Meiosis & Variation
points: Meiosis I: Homologous chromosomes separate (halves chromosome number: 2n → n). Crossing over (chiasmata) exchanges alleles; independent segregation creates new maternal/paternal combinations.
Meiosis II: Sister chromatids separate.
Non-disjunction: Failure of homologous chromosomes or chromatids to separate → aneuploidy.

3.4.4.title: Topic 3.4.4 · Genetic Diversity & Natural Selection
3.4.4.spec: Directional and stabilising selection, antibiotic resistance

sections.heading: Natural Selection
points: 1. Variation exists in a population due to random mutation.
2. Selection pressure means individuals with advantageous alleles are more likely to survive and reproduce.
3. Advantageous alleles are passed to offspring; allele frequency increases over generations.
Directional selection: Favours one extreme (e.g. antibiotic resistance). Stabilising selection: Favours the mean (e.g. human birth weight).

3.4.5.title: Topic 3.4.5 · Species and Taxonomy
3.4.5.spec: Species definition, courtship behaviour, phylogenetic classification, DKPCOFGS

sections.heading: Classification & Courtship
points: Species: Group of organisms able to interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
Courtship behaviour: Recognise own species, identify mate capable of breeding, form pair bond, synchronise mating.
Taxonomy: Hierarchical (no overlap), phylogenetic (based on evolutionary relationships): Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

3.4.6.title: Topic 3.4.6 · Biodiversity within a Community
3.4.6.spec: Species richness, Simpson's Index of Diversity, farming impacts

sections.heading: Index of Diversity
points: Formula: D = N(N − 1) / Σn(n − 1), where N = total number of organisms of all species, n = total number of organisms of each species.
Agriculture: Monoculture, hedgerow removal, pesticides/herbicides reduce biodiversity; conservation schemes (wildflower strips, hedgerows) restore it.

3.4.7.title: Topic 3.4.7 · Investigating Diversity
3.4.7.spec: DNA/mRNA/amino acid sequencing, random sampling, standard deviation

sections.heading: Measuring Diversity
points: Molecular comparison: Compare DNA base sequences, mRNA sequences, or amino acid sequences (fewer differences = more closely related).
Sampling: Random sampling (random number generator + grid) avoids bias; large sample size increases reliability; mean ± standard deviation shows spread around the mean.

3.5.1.title: Topic 3.5.1 · Photosynthesis
3.5.1.spec: Light-dependent reaction (thylakoids), Calvin cycle (stroma), limiting factors

sections.heading: Light-Dependent & Light-Independent Reactions
points: Light-dependent (thylakoid membranes): Photoionisation of chlorophyll → e- transport chain → H+ pumped into thylakoid lumen → chemiosmosis via ATP synthase → ATP + reduced NADP. Photolysis: 2H2O → 4H+ + 4e- + O2.
Calvin cycle (stroma): CO2 + RuBP (5C) → 2 GP (3C) via Rubisco → reduced to 2 TP (3C) using ATP and reduced NADP → 1/6 TP forms hexose/organic molecules, 5/6 regenerates RuBP using ATP.

3.5.2.title: Topic 3.5.2 · Respiration
3.5.2.spec: Glycolysis, link reaction, Krebs cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, anaerobic respiration

sections.heading: Aerobic & Anaerobic Respiration
points: Glycolysis (cytoplasm): Glucose (6C) → 2 pyruvate (3C) + net 2 ATP + 2 reduced NAD.
Link reaction (mitochondrial matrix): Pyruvate → acetyl CoA (2C) + CO2 + reduced NAD.
Krebs cycle (matrix): Acetyl CoA + oxaloacetate (4C) → citrate (6C) → regenerates 4C, yielding 2 CO2, 1 ATP (substrate-level), 3 reduced NAD, 1 reduced FAD per turn.
Oxidative phosphorylation (cristae): Reduced NAD/FAD donate e- to ETC → H+ pumped to intermembrane space → chemiosmosis via ATP synthase. O2 is terminal electron acceptor (forms H2O).
Anaerobic: Regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis continues (animals: lactate; plants/yeast: ethanol + CO2).

3.5.3.title: Topic 3.5.3 · Energy and Ecosystems
3.5.3.spec: GPP, NPP = GPP - R, net production of consumers N = I - (F + R), farming efficiency

sections.heading: Productivity & Energy Transfer
points: NPP = GPP − R (Net Primary Production = Gross Primary Production minus respiratory losses).
Consumers: N = I − (F + R) (I = chemical energy in ingested food, F = faeces/urine, R = respiration).
Efficiency: % efficiency = (Energy after transfer / Energy before transfer) × 100. Simplifying food webs and restricting movement/heating increases efficiency.

3.5.4.title: Topic 3.5.4 · Nutrient Cycles
3.5.4.spec: Nitrogen cycle, phosphorus cycle, mycorrhizae, fertilisers, eutrophication

sections.heading: Nitrogen, Phosphorus & Eutrophication
points: Nitrogen cycle: Nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium: N2 → NH3), ammonification (saprobionts), nitrification (NH4+ → NO2- → NO3-, aerobic), denitrification (NO3- → N2, anaerobic/waterlogged).
Mycorrhizae: Symbiotic fungi on plant roots increase SA for water and mineral (especially phosphate) uptake.
Eutrophication: Leaching of nitrates/phosphates → algal bloom → blocks light → plants die → saprobionts decompose & respire aerobically → O2 depleted → fish die.

3.6.1.title: Topic 3.6.1 · Stimuli, Receptors & Tropisms
3.6.1.spec: Taxes, kineses, IAA phototropism/gravitropism, Pacinian corpuscle, rods & cones, heart rate control

sections.heading: Responses & Receptors
points: Taxis: Directional movement towards/away from stimulus. Kinesis: Non-directional change in speed/turning rate.
IAA (plant): Promotes cell elongation in shoots, inhibits in roots.
Pacinian corpuscle: Mechanical pressure deforms lamellae → opens stretch-mediated Na+ channels → generator potential.
Rods vs Cones: Rods (rhodopsin, high sensitivity/low acuity via summation, black & white); Cones (iodopsin, low sensitivity/high acuity, 1:1 bipolar connection, colour).
Heart rate: Chemoreceptors/baroreceptors → medulla oblongata → sympathetic (noradrenaline, SAN ↑) or parasympathetic (acetylcholine, SAN ↓).

3.6.2.title: Topic 3.6.2 · Nervous Coordination & Synapses
3.6.2.spec: Resting potential, action potential, myelination/saltatory conduction, cholinergic synapses

sections.heading: Action Potentials & Synapses
points: Resting potential (-70 mV): Na+/K+ pump (3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in) + higher K+ permeability.

Action potential: Threshold reached → voltage-gated Na+ channels open (depolarisation to +40 mV) → Na+ close, K+ open (repolarisation → hyperpolarisation). Refractory period ensures unidirectional propagation.
Saltatory conduction: Myelinated axons depolarise only at Nodes of Ranvier → faster.
Cholinergic synapse: AP arrives → Ca2+ channels open → vesicles fuse & release ACh → binds postsynaptic receptors → Na+ influx → EPSP; acetylcholinesterase hydrolyses ACh.

3.6.3.title: Topic 3.6.3 · Skeletal Muscles
3.6.3.spec: Sliding filament theory, sarcomere bands, phosphocreatine, slow vs fast twitch fibres

sections.heading: Sliding Filament Theory
points: Sarcomere: Z-line to Z-line. During contraction: I-band & H-zone shorten; A-band stays same width.

Mechanism: Ca2+ released from sarcoplasmic reticulum binds troponin → tropomyosin moves, exposing actin binding sites → myosin heads form cross-bridges → power stroke (ADP + Pi released) → ATP binds myosin to detach & hydrolyses to recock.
Phosphocreatine: Rapidly donates phosphate to ADP to regenerate ATP in fast-twitch fibres.

3.6.4.title: Topic 3.6.4 · Homeostasis
3.6.4.spec: Negative feedback, insulin/glucagon/adrenaline, nephron, Loop of Henle, ADH

sections.heading: Blood Glucose & Osmoregulation
points: Insulin (β-cells): Increases glucose uptake (GLUT4), glycogenesis, respiration. Glucagon (α-cells): Glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis (second messenger cAMP).
Kidney: Ultrafiltration at Bowman's capsule; selective reabsorption of glucose in PCT; Loop of Henle countercurrent multiplier creates low Ψ in medulla.
ADH: Released from posterior pituitary when osmoreceptors in hypothalamus shrink → increases aquaporins in DCT/collecting duct → more water reabsorbed.

3.7.1.title: Topic 3.7.1 · Inheritance & Chi-Squared
3.7.1.spec: Monohybrid, dihybrid, codominance, sex-linkage, autosomal linkage, epistasis, chi-squared

sections.heading: Genetic Crosses & Chi-Squared
points: Classic F2 ratios: Monohybrid 3:1; Dihybrid 9:3:3:1; Codominance 1:2:1; Epistasis (9:3:4, 12:3:1, 9:7).
Autosomal linkage: Genes on same chromosome inherited together unless separated by crossing over.
Chi-squared (χ2): Σ[(O − E)2 / E]. Compare to critical value at p = 0.05 with df = n − 1. If χ2 ≥ critical, reject null hypothesis.

3.7.2.title: Topic 3.7.2 · Populations & Hardy-Weinberg
3.7.2.spec: Gene pool, allele frequency, Hardy-Weinberg equations and assumptions

sections.heading: Hardy-Weinberg Principle
points: Equations: p + q = 1 and p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1 (p = dominant allele, q = recessive allele, 2pq = heterozygotes).
Assumptions: Large population, random mating, no mutations, no selection, no migration (gene flow).

3.7.3.title: Topic 3.7.3 · Evolution & Speciation
3.7.3.spec: Directional/stabilising/disruptive selection, allopatric & sympatric speciation, genetic drift

sections.heading: Speciation & Genetic Drift
points: Allopatric speciation: Geographical isolation → different selection pressures + mutations → reproductive isolation.
Sympatric speciation: Reproductive isolation within same area (e.g. behavioural, temporal, polyploidy).
Genetic drift: Random change in allele frequency, strongest in small populations.

3.7.4.title: Topic 3.7.4 · Populations in Ecosystems & Succession
3.7.4.spec: Carrying capacity, predator-prey, quadrats, mark-release-recapture, primary/secondary succession

sections.heading: Ecology & Sampling
points: Mark-release-recapture (Lincoln Index): N = (n1 × n2) / m. Assumes no births/deaths/migration, marks don't harm or rub off, random mixing.
Primary succession: Pioneer species colonise bare rock → alter abiotic conditions (humus/soil) → seral stages → climax community (higher biodiversity & biomass).

sections.heading: Types of Mutation
points: Substitution: May be silent (degenerate code), missense (different amino acid), or nonsense (premature stop codon).
Deletion / Insertion: Causes a frameshift, altering every downstream codon and amino acid sequence.

3.8.2.title: Topic 3.8.2 · Regulation of Gene Expression & Cancer
3.8.2.spec: Stem cells (totipotent/pluripotent/multipotent/iPS), transcription factors, epigenetics, RNAi, oncogenes

sections.heading: Stem Cells, Epigenetics & Cancer
points: Stem cells: Totipotent (any cell + placenta), Pluripotent (any body cell, e.g. ESCs), Multipotent/Unipotent (adult). iPS cells reprogrammed from adult somatic cells.
Oestrogen: Lipid-soluble → binds cytoplasmic receptor → transcription factor enters nucleus & activates transcription.
Epigenetics: Increased DNA methylation (inhibits transcription) and decreased histone acetylation (tighter chromatin, inhibits transcription).
RNAi: siRNA/miRNA binds RISC and cleaves or blocks mRNA translation.
Cancer: Mutated proto-oncogenes → oncogenes (permanently active cell division); mutated/hypermethylated tumour suppressor genes (loss of inhibition).

3.8.3.title: Topic 3.8.3 · Genome Projects
3.8.3.spec: Sequencing genomes, determining proteome in prokaryotes vs eukaryotes

sections.heading: Genomes & Proteomes
points: Prokaryotes: Few/no introns → proteome easily determined from genome.
Eukaryotes: Extensive non-coding DNA and regulatory sequences make predicting the proteome from the genome much harder.

3.8.4.title: Topic 3.8.4 · Gene Technologies & Genetic Fingerprinting
3.8.4.spec: Reverse transcriptase, restriction endonucleases, in vivo cloning, PCR, DNA probes, VNTRs

sections.heading: Recombinant DNA, PCR & Fingerprinting
points: Obtaining DNA: Reverse transcriptase (mRNA → cDNA), restriction endonucleases (sticky/blunt ends), gene machine.
In vivo cloning: Vector (plasmid) + DNA ligase → transformation (Ca2+ + heat shock) → marker genes (antibiotic resistance/GFP).
PCR (in vitro): 95°C (denature), ~55°C (anneal primers), 72°C (Taq polymerase extends).
Genetic fingerprinting: Cut DNA with restriction enzymes → gel electrophoresis separates VNTRs by size → Southern blot → labelled DNA probes hybridise.

RP.title: Required Practicals (RP1–RP12)
RP.spec: All 12 AQA AS & A-Level Biology Required Practicals

sections.heading: AS Required Practicals (RP1–RP6)
points: RP1: Effect of a named variable on rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction (e.g. trypsin + milk powder, colorimeter).
RP2: Preparation of stained squashes of cells from plant root tips; set-up and use of optical microscope to calculate mitotic index.
RP3: Dilution series of a solute to produce a calibration curve to identify water potential of plant tissue (potato cylinders, % change in mass).
RP4: Effect of a named variable on permeability of cell-surface membranes (beetroot pigment leakage, colorimeter).
RP5: Dissection of animal/plant gas exchange or mass transport system (heart, fish gills, insect).
RP6: Use of aseptic techniques to investigate effect of antimicrobial substances on microbial growth (zone of inhibition).

sections.heading: A-Level Required Practicals (RP7–RP12)
points: RP7: Use of chromatography to investigate pigments isolated from leaves of different plants (Rf = distance moved by pigment / distance moved by solvent front).
RP8: Effect of ammonium hydroxide / light / DCPIP on dehydrogenase activity in chloroplasts (Hill reaction, colorimeter).
RP9: Effect of a named variable on rate of respiration of cultures of single-celled organisms (yeast + methylene blue / redox indicator).
RP10: Effect of an environmental variable on movement of an animal using a choice chamber or maze (chi-squared test).
RP11: Production of a dilution series of a glucose solution and use of colorimetric techniques to produce a calibration curve to identify concentration of glucose in an unknown 'urine' sample.
RP12: Investigation into the effect of a named environmental factor on the distribution of a given species (belt transect / random quadrats).
